page: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-75s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. Operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The system is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 75 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also show strong performance, with gzip compression reaching 31.28 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.57 GB/sec. However, multi-core and multi-threaded scaling present tradeoffs; stress-ng multi-core performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression drops to the bottom 25%. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is strong at 120.89 GB/sec, whereas read bandwidth remains average.

Due to the shared CPU allocation, this instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require dedicated physical cores. It is suitable for single-threaded processing, lightweight LLM inference using small models, and basic Redis key-value operations. It is less suited for heavy database operations or high-throughput static web serving, where benchmarks indicate weaker performance.
